ig_carousel_topic.topic: Why anyone claiming an 80% win rate is lying or selling something
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Someone's claiming 80% win rate.
That's not a service. That's a warning sign.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: Most bettors assume a good tipster hits 70, 80, even 90 percent. Sportsbooks exist because that's not how this works. Vegas sets lines specifically to make 50-50 feel like a coin flip.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: The honest target is 53 to 58 percent. At 55% on standard -110 juice, you're profitable. At 80%, you'd be the richest person in sports history within two seasons. No one is 80%.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text: Real math: 100 bets at $100 each, -110 juice. You need 52.4 wins just to break even. At 55% you net roughly $450. At 80% you'd net over $7,000. No public tipster sustains that. Ever.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: 54.3% across 490 graded picks is what verified looks like. Not flashy. Profitable. Anyone showing you 80% is either cherry-picking a 10-bet sample or fabricating results.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: 80% win rate claims are a red flag, not a selling point. Real edge looks like 54-57%. Here's the math that exposes the fraud.
